title: Flatness and local finite presentation descend through a smooth source cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $A\xrightarrow{h}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ be morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$, both representable by algebraic spaces. Suppose $h$ is smooth and surjective. Then $g$ is flat if $gh$ is flat, and $g$ is locally of finite presentation if $gh$ is locally of finite presentation. These two assertions are separate and require no quasi-compactness of $h$. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, 2-fibre products, and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness, flatness and local finite presentation are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Surjectivity means that every field-valued point of the target lifts after some extension of its field.

source.place: Tag 06M2 (lemma-check-property-after-precomposing), tau=smooth; source locality of flatness and local finite presentation: Tags 06ET (lemma-flat-fpqc-local-source) and 06EV (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-fppf-local-source).

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and a map $T\to C$. Set $Y=B\times_C T$ and $X=A\times_C T$. Representability of $g$ makes $Y$ an algebraic space. The canonical equivalence $X\simeq Y\times_B A$ and [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space], applied to $h$ and $Y\to B$, make $X$ an algebraic space too. Thus $gh$ is representable as well. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], the base change $p:X\to Y$ of $h$ is smooth and surjective. Write $P$ for flatness or, separately, local finite presentation, and suppose $gh$ has $P$. The defining scheme-base-change test gives $P(X\to T)$.

source.place: Tag 06M2, lemma-check-property-after-precomposing, proof: scheme base change; algebraic.tex Tag 0300

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $a:U\to Y$, and put $W=X\times_Y U$. This is an algebraic space by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space], applied to $p$ and $U\to Y$. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $b:V\to W$. The chartwise calculus shows that $W\to U$ is smooth and surjective, $W\to X$ is etale, and hence the scheme map $v:V\to U$ is smooth and surjective. In particular $v$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The composite $V\to W\to X\to T$ has $P$: its first two maps are etale and therefore have $P$, and $X\to T$ has $P$. These assertions use base change and composition from [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; their agreement with the scheme notions is the scheme comparison in [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], using [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. If $f:U\to T$ is induced by $Y\to T$, associativity of the fibre products identifies that composite with $f\circ v$.

In the flatness case apply [lem-pc-flat-source-descent] to the scheme maps $V\xrightarrow{v}U\xrightarrow{f}T$: $v$ is flat and surjective and $fv$ is flat, so $f$ is flat. In the local-finite-presentation case use the singleton family $\{v:V\to U\}$ in [lem-trf-lfp-fppf-source-locality]: $v$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective, and $fv$ is locally of finite presentation, so $f$ is locally of finite presentation. The flatness argument has not assumed $gh$ to be locally of finite presentation, and the latter argument has not assumed $gh$ to be flat.

For either choice of $P$, [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] says that $P$ is etale local on source-and-target. In [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] use the presentation diagram for $Y\to T$ with source $U\to Y$, target $\operatorname{id}_T$, and scheme map $f:U\to T$. Its source chart is surjective and $P(f)$ was proved, so $Y\to T$ has $P$. This holds for every scheme $T\to C$, hence $g$ has $P$ by its defining test. No step required either chart or $h$ to be quasi-compact; the two scheme descent statements used in step 3 impose no such hypothesis.
